name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons

significance.quote: the observed (expected) significance amounts to 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations

summary.plain: ATLAS saw, on its own, the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau leptons - heavy cousins of the electron - confirming that the Higgs couples to this type of particle.
summary.technical: Combination of boosted-Higgs and VBF categories using 13 TeV data (36.1 fb^-1): observed (expected) significance 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations for H -> tau tau, an ATLAS-only observation.

title: Cross-section measurements of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau-leptons in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: It was ATLAS's own first observation of the Higgs boson coupling directly to leptons, testing the Yukawa-coupling structure of the Standard Model in a second fermion channel after b quarks and top quarks.
